judgments.reasoning_cat1: The removal right is clear and symmetrical, but this section is also numbered "Section 6.6", duplicating the preceding compensation section, and "Unless otherwise restricted by Law" invokes the over-broad "Laws" definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Section 6.1's vacancy-filling rule (LSB fills the LSB seat, DMSA the DMSA seats); the duplicate numbering is cushioned by Section 1.2's headings clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short agency statement limited to "the extent of their powers set forth in this Agreement"; nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 7.6 for Officers and Section 6.8's limits on what Directors may do.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (iii) — barring "any distributions to Members other than to reimburse DMSA for initial capital contributions" — is a striking one-sided carve-out whose scope (does it permit that reimbursement, or merely exempt it from unanimity?) is genuinely uncertain, and the list ends with the open-ended "any material liability or obligation".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (iii) cannot be squared with Section 9.1 (Net Cash Flow distributed in proportion to Percentage Interests), Section 9.2 (Board sets amounts) or Section 4.3(ii)(b) (Members paid profits per their interests), and it favours DMSA alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional officer provisions; "shall hold office until their successors are chosen and qualify" is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Officer removal by majority Board vote here sits against Section 6.8(x), which requires unanimity for terminating Officer employment contracts — office and contract are distinguishable but the line is thin.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "general and active management of the business of the Company" is a broad grant, but it is the standard corporate-president formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Section 6.1 (Board manages the business and affairs) and Section 6.8's unanimity list; the President's contracting power is expressly qualified, which harmonises them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard succession provision, conditional on there being a Vice President at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.2's cross-reference to Section 7.3 matches; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and conventional duties; nothing ambiguous in the wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the "Secretary" definition, Section 2.1(iii) and Section 2.6; the Secretary's Schedule A updating power is the only sensitive interaction and it lives in 2.1(iii).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional treasurer duties; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article X's books and records requirements and Section 6.8(xi).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short agency statement bounded by the Officers' conferred powers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Section 6.7 for Directors; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "the fiduciary duty of loyalty and care similar to those of directors and officers of business corporations" imports an external standard by analogy — "similar to" is imprecise — and the opening "Except to the extent provided herein" leaves the carve-outs unidentified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.7 expressly relieves DMSA of its fiduciary duties as a Director and Section 12.3 replaces duties existing at law, so the scope of the duty this section imposes turns entirely on those other provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two parallel sentences allocating Profits and Losses by Percentage Interest; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 8.2, 9.1 and Schedule A's 51/49 split; only the thin §703(a) Profits definition creates any friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (ii)'s "in the same proportions as they shared Interest Profits and Losses" is garbled — "Interest" has been substituted for "share" — and the limb numbering repeats "(i)".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The intended reference is plainly the Percentage Interest allocation in Section 8.1, and clause (iv)'s §704(b) intent sits against the bare §703(a) Profits definition and Section 4.4(ii).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A boilerplate §704(c) provision that leaves the allocation method unspecified but tracks the statute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coherent with Sections 8.1, 8.2 and 4.4(ii); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One clear sentence: Net Cash Flow distributions are made in proportion to Percentage Interests.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.8(iii) bars "any distributions to Members other than to reimburse DMSA for initial capital contributions" without unanimous Board approval, which is hard to reconcile with a pro-rata entitlement stated here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short delegation of timing and amount to the Board; the discretion is unqualified but plainly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It gives the Board control while the Net Cash Flow definition gives the Members the reserve determination, and Section 6.8(iii) subjects distributions to unanimity — three different gatekeepers for one decision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear legal-compliance limitation using the defined term "Law".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates the similar restriction in Section 4.3(i) on returns of capital; complementary rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard withholding provision; the internal reference "pursuant to this 9.4" is missing the word "Section" but the meaning is unaffected.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 9.1 and 11.2; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "together with a copy of this Agreement and of the Certificate" uses "Certificate", a term the Agreement never defines, and the inspection right for "any purpose reasonably related to such Member's interest" is a standard but elastic limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement defines "Articles", not "Certificate" (see Article I and Section 2.1(iv)), so the record-keeping obligation refers to a document that does not exist as defined.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It mandates the accrual method "for both financial and tax reporting purposes", which is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Net Cash Flow definition requires determination "in accordance with the cash receipts and disbursements method of accounting" — a direct clash of prescribed accounting methods.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear designation and a specific ten-day notice duty; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 11.2's partnership treatment and Article X's tax-return duties.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence tax election statement; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coherent with Articles VIII and XI throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard statutory liability shield, expressly subject to the Maine Act.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.4 (indemnity out of Company assets only) and 15.5 (no recourse against other Members).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section is visibly truncated: after clause (i) the text jumps to a fragment beginning "professional or expert competence and who has been selected with reasonable care", with no subject or operative verb — a missing clause (ii) reliance provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The lost reliance protection is presupposed by Sections 12.3 and 12.4, so the exculpation scheme cannot be read whole as printed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "good faith reliance on the provisions of this Agreement" is a narrow protection expressed in ordinary fiduciary language; the replacement of duties is stated squarely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.7 imposes corporate-style loyalty and care duties "except to the extent provided herein" while this section replaces duties existing at law, and Section 12.7 releases DMSA specifically — the three together leave the actual duty standard contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A carefully drafted indemnity with an express good-faith condition and gross negligence/willful misconduct carve-out; long but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 17.11 confines rights under the Agreement to Members and Managers, yet "Covered Person" extends indemnity to employees, agents and Affiliates who are neither.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard advancement clause with an undertaking to repay; the terminal sentence lacks its full stop but nothing turns on it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on Section 12.4, which is intact, but inherits the same Covered Person/Section 17.11 tension over who may enforce it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision breaks off mid-sentence at "against any liability that may be asserted", so the scope of the insurance permission is literally incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The missing tail would have tied the insurance to acts in the Covered Person's capacity, linking it to Sections 12.4 and 12.5; as printed the connection must be supplied by inference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is textually broken ("and the Company the income or profits derived therefrom" has no verb) and its operative restraint on LSB turns on "such services" — which has no antecedent — and "the business", an undefined and unbounded reference; it is also drafted wholly one-sidedly in DMSA's favour.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its release of DMSA's fiduciary duties contradicts Section 7.7's imposition of loyalty and care on every Director, and the reach of LSB's exclusivity depends entirely on Section 3.1's dual purpose statement (Spanish-language newspapers plus "any lawful act or activity").

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "all efforts and actions undertaken by them for the Company... are to be kept confidential" is far broader and vaguer than the defined "Proprietary Information" that follows, and consent must come from "the LLC", a body the Agreement never defines (the defined term is "Company").
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Proprietary Information list overlaps the exclusivity restraint in Section 12.7 and the DMSA competition safe harbour in the same section, raising the question how DMSA can compete freely while bound by this confidentiality covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear two-condition admission mechanic requiring approval of all Members.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the "Additional Members" definition, Section 15.1 and Section 16.3; the Company bearing legal fees is a small commercial term, not a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "entitled to their respective Interest of the Company's income" repeats the document's "Interest"/"share" substitution, making the entitlement formula read oddly against the defined term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses a different allocation vocabulary from Sections 8.1 and 8.2, though the substance (pro-rata post-admission allocations) is reconcilable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "without complying with the terms of this Agreement" is circular — the section prohibits assignment by reference to unspecified terms elsewhere rather than stating any standard of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The applicable restrictions live in Article XVI (Sections 16.2, 16.3, 16.5 and 16.6) rather than Article XIV, and Section 14.2 refers to violations "of this Article XIV", so the two articles' interaction is genuinely loose.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It voids assignments "in violation of this Article XIV", but Article XIV itself imposes almost no substantive restriction beyond the circular Section 14.1.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The real transfer restrictions sit in Article XVI, so a transfer breaching Article XVI is not literally caught by this invalidating provision — a gap between the two articles.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, absolute prohibition requiring prior written consent of all Members; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.8 lets the Board unilaterally waive "any transfer restrictions contained in this Agreement", which would let a Board majority override the unanimous-Member consent this section demands.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One clear negative proposition about admissions not causing dissolution.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 13.1 and 15.2; the reference to "substitute Members" is used without a definition but is intelligible.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of dissolution triggers is enumerated and closed, but "retirement" and "expulsion" appear with no mechanism anywhere in the Agreement for either.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (ii) treats "resignation" of a Member as a dissolution event although Section 5.4 flatly forbids a Member from resigning, and the "all of the remaining Members agree" cure is awkward in a two-member company given the "Members" definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The Members shall continue to distribute Interest Profits and Losses during liquidation" is garbled — Members do not distribute, and "Interest Profits" is not a defined term — and "a reasonable time... for the orderly liquidation" is elastic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Liquidating distributions here follow Capital Account balances, whereas Section 9.1 distributes by Percentage Interests, and Schedule A's contribution figures make those two measures diverge sharply.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear two-condition termination statement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.3, 15.3 and the Maine Act cancellation requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The look-solely-to-Company-assets formula is standard and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.1, 12.4 and 4.3(iii); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Each transfer of Interests of the Company shall be made on Schedule A" is a curious formulation — a schedule entry as the mode of transfer rather than its record.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Section 2.1(iii), under which the Secretary may update Schedule A and such updates are not amendments, which would let record ownership shift outside the Article XVI process.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of "transfer" is exhaustively enumerated with one express carve-out, and the sanctions (no vote, no distribution) are specific; the phrase "restrictions on transfer set forth below" is the only loose reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Set forth below" points to Sections 16.3 to 16.8, one of which (16.4) is truncated and cross-refers to non-existent Sections 16.9 to 16.11 — so the body of restrictions incorporated is incomplete.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear validity condition on transferees joining the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 13.1's admission mechanic and Section 16.2; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision is a fragment — it stops at "the Company and the other Members shall" with no predicate — and it invokes Sections 16.9, 16.10 and 16.11, none of which exist in the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article XVI ends at Section 16.8, so this waiver provision refers to a transfer regime the instrument never contains, leaving Section 16.2's "restrictions set forth below" incomplete.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "in form and substance Satisfactory to the Board or the President" and waiver "for good cause" are both discretionary standards without a reasonableness qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Waiver power is given here to the Board or the President individually, while Section 16.8 requires a duly adopted Board resolution for any waiver of transfer restrictions — an inconsistency about who may waive.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The right of first refusal is mechanically defective: it refers to "LLC Votes", a term never defined (the defined term is Member Votes); it fixes no period within which the offer may be accepted yet later speaks of "the periods set forth above"; and the over-subscription sentence compares "aggregate Interests offered to be purchased" with "the number to be transferred" incoherently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The missing acceptance period leaves Section 16.2's compliance sanctions unworkable, and the Board's allocation discretion here sits against Section 16.8's waiver power and Section 14.3's unanimity requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "such additional rules and regulations as it deems expedient" is broad but expressly bounded by consistency with the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "not inconsistent with this Agreement" limit harmonises it with Article XVI generally; no specific conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary" plus a power to waive "any transfer restrictions contained in this Agreement" if the Board "deems" waiver in the Company's best interests is an unusually unfettered, subjective discretion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It lets a Board majority override Section 14.3's requirement of unanimous Member consent to a pledge and the Section 16.6 right of first refusal — the sort of provision that, read literally, nullifies protections elsewhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of delivery methods is specific and closed, and "deemed to have been given when received" is a clear rule; no notice address is provided for the Company beyond a cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cross-reference to Section 2.5 is accurate, but that section lets the Board relocate the principal place of business at any time, so the notice address is a moving target.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is mangled: a non-waiver clause should say the failure to insist shall not prevent a subsequent act from having the effect of an original violation, and the printed text drops the necessary negative structure, leaving the meaning contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Section 17.3 (cumulative remedies) the intended non-waiver effect is recoverable, but the clause as written may say something close to the opposite of what a non-waiver clause does.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional cumulative-remedies clause; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements Section 17.2 and does not conflict with any exculpation or indemnity provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard successors-and-assigns clause with an internal limitation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "to the extent permitted by this Agreement" qualifier expressly defers to Articles XIV and XVI; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A boilerplate gender-and-number clause; no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its statement that all references to Sections refer to corresponding provisions of this Agreement is undercut by the dangling references to Sections 6.9, 16.9, 16.10 and 16.11, which have no corresponding provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard severability with a stray full stop mid-sentence; meaning unaffected.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflict with any other provision located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard counterparts clause; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.1(ii) and 13.1, which contemplate execution of counterparts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short integration clause limited to "the subject matter hereof", a boundary that is not self-defining.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.3(ii)(a) contemplates DMSA invoicing the Company under separate service arrangements, so whether those dealings fall within "the subject matter hereof" and are superseded is genuinely open.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear Maine choice-of-law clause expressly excluding conflicts principles; it covers interpretation and remedies but not forum.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Maine Act references throughout and with Section 7.7's reference to the Maine Business Corporation Act, notwithstanding the Massachusetts principal place of business in Section 2.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The unanimity and writing requirements are stated clearly, though "affirmative vote of all of the Members" and "executed by all of the Members" are cumulative in an unusual way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(iii) declares that revisions to Schedule A — which fixes Percentage Interests and Member Votes — are not amendments, so economic terms can change without the unanimity this section demands.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out "except the Members and Managers" is a closed list that omits Directors, Officers and other Covered Persons, an expressio unius problem in a document that grants them rights.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 12.4 and 12.5 confer indemnity and expense advancement on every Covered Person, including employees, agents and Affiliates who are neither Members nor Managers — this section would deny them any remedy.
